title: Stale-baseline check: nested test classes undercount, and the baseline-only scope survives as a mutant
description:
Filed from the TS-27 round-2 review (Sonnet unit, APPROVE), which recorded two known limits and one surviving mutant that were not asked for under the cap of 84.

1. gate.py _collected_ids: a nested test class A::B::test normalises to mod.A::B::test, while JUnit reports classname mod.A.B. The ids never intersect, so a suite with nested classes undercounts and is falsely refused. It fails closed, not open.
2. tests/test_gate.py pass fixture: a scope built from the baseline ids alone would also pass it, because the deselected test is in neither the run nor the baseline. The run-ids-only mutant, the unscoped mutant and the compare-skip mutant each turn something red; this one survives.
3. The union in the stale check can hide a stale baseline where a PR removes or renames base tests the baseline does not list AND its JUnit omits exactly those ids. Narrow and PR-supplied; recorded on TS-27 as a known limit. No test is asked for here.

Do not start this by sizing tests: every case it needs is a measured slot request to the leader, sized with the #13 amendment under DEC-195 (4).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A base tree with nested test classes measures the ids JUnit reports for them (mod.A.B::test), so the measurement and the run intersect instead of undercounting to a false refusal.
A case in the suite distinguishes the shipped scope from one built from the baseline test_ids alone, so a mutation to the baseline-only scope turns that case red.

implementationNotes: DELIVERED 2026-10-20. Item 1, nested test classes: fixed in gate.py _collected_ids, which now folds every leading class segment into the module rather than one, so file::A::B::test normalises to mod.A.B::test, the form JUnit reports (classname mod.A.B, name test). The parameter guard is unchanged in effect: a segment carrying a bracket ends the class path, so test_p[a::b] is still one name. Proved both arms on the existing case test_collected_ids_folds_a_class_into_the_module_part, extended with a nested-class id and NO new collected case (cap untouched at 95 of 95): the while fold passes, the single if fails. Item 2, baseline-only scope mutant: NOT REPRODUCIBLE on the current tree. I applied the mutation by hand at gate.py:428 (measured intersected with (run ids union baseline ids) reduced to baseline ids alone), cleared pycache, and ran the suite: test_a_baseline_that_does_not_match_the_base_count_fails_by_name[0] and [2] both go red. An existing case therefore already distinguishes the shipped scope from the baseline-only one, so that AC is met without a new case. Item 3, the narrow union case: its description asked for no test and none was added.
